Token-Head Feature Atlas

What the frozen Unified-28 token head reads, how its seven per-token streams behave over generation time, what the IU-PCR evidence curve looks like on real error traces, and whether the token-level correlation structure matches the IU-PCR, SU-PCR, or dependency-aware fusion models.
2026-08-28 · descriptive / diagnostic only — no frozen method is changed, selected, or promoted · frozen model base7_full28 (artifact SHA-256 49168791e0687a23…) · data: ProcessBench Llama-3.1-8B (GSM8K 400 + MATH 300), RAGTruth-EC pilot
Findings at a glance
  • Every stream spikes exactly at the first-error onset and stays elevated afterwards; the frozen IU-PCR evidence inherits both the spike and the sustained shift. neg_logsumexp is unique: on wrong traces it keeps rising through the trace instead of decaying.
  • The token-level correlation structure is dense low-rank, not sparse: two components carry 81% of the off-diagonal energy (λ = 15.0, 5.7, 2.6…), and SU-PCR’s sparse-error decomposition finds zero sparse pairs — on this matrix SU-PCR collapses to IU-PCR (cosine 1.000). The two-component IU-PCR choice is exactly right for the low-rank part.
  • The conditional-independence reading fails at token level: conditioning on the token label leaves mean |ρ| unchanged (0.484 → 0.479 / 0.498). The correlation is feature redundancy, not label-driven signal — the structural argument for dependency-aware fusion (the DEEM line), and simultaneously a warning that the leading PC is a redundancy axis, not the signal axis.
  • The redundancy blocks are organized by transform, not by stream: same-transform mean |ρ| = 0.87 vs same-stream 0.50 vs neither 0.45. The seven streams are near-interchangeable copies of one uncertainty signal; the four temporal transforms are what actually diversify the pool.
  • Descriptively, the frozen head is hard to beat with same-representation refits: frozen weights lead every diagnostic (token AUROC 0.543, exact step hit 0.329, within-1 0.608); a simple average is the closest challenger; the dependency-corrected SDSF ridge inverts weights and loses badly.
Section 1

What the token head reads

The frozen token/local head (base7_full28, the Unified-28 method of record) fuses 28 causal coordinates: seven registered risk-oriented streams × four causal transforms. Each coordinate is robust-standardized against the frozen fit reference (median/IQR, clipped ±8), oriented so higher = riskier, and combined by frozen two-component L2 IU-PCR weights into one evidence value per token. With the Identity accumulator, risk = evidence, the localization answer is argmaxt evidence, and the global score is simply the evidence at the final token — the cumulative transforms carry the whole-trace summary.

StreamFormula (risk orientation: higher = riskier)Raw source
entropysaved per-token Shannon entropy H(n)token_entropies
neg_logsumexp−logsumexp(logits) — negative energytoken_logsumexp
neg_top1−log p(top-1 token)top_k_logprobs
topk_entropy−Σ p log p over the renormalized top-50top_k_logprobs
topk_varentropyΣ p (−log p − E[−log p])²top_k_logprobs
topk_renyi2−log Σ p² (collision / Rényi-2 entropy)top_k_logprobs
topk_tail_massclip(1 − Σi≤5 pi, 0, 1)top_k_logprobs

Two of the nine registered raw channels are deliberately not in the head (spilled = −log p(sampled token), neg_margin = −(top1−top2)); they were dropped by the frozen base7 selection. The four causal transforms are: level (the standardized instantaneous value), ewma16 (EWMA, α=2/17), positive_area (running mean of max(v,0) since t=0), and persistence (running fraction of tokens with v>0). Level and ewma16 are local; positive_area and persistence are cumulative — they encode history.

Section 3

The IU-PCR token-head output around the first error

Two properties of the evidence curve matter for the fusion work. First, the signal is event-like, not level-like: per-trace token AUROC of the frozen evidence against the first-error-step mask is only 0.549 at the median (IQR 0.438–0.668, n=395 error traces) — the head does not separate error tokens from clean tokens wholesale; it localizes because the largest spike tends to co-occur with the error onset. Second, the sustained post-onset shift means late tokens in a wrong trace are all mildly elevated — which is exactly what the global head (evidence at the last token) feeds on, but which also blurs the localization argmax toward late high-entropy tokens (the gsm8k-14 miss in Fig 2).

Section 5

Does the structure match IU-PCR, SU-PCR, or something else?

ModelAssumed covariance mechanismDiagnostic on this token matrixVerdict
IU-PCR (deployed config)diagonal + rank-2 2 components used; rank-2 removes 81% of off-diagonal energy; λ²-fraction 0.22 (second component is real); projection residual 0.053; ρ̂ range 0.19–0.72 Good fit for the low-rank part. The two-component choice is exactly the knee of the spectrum.
SU-PCR (sparse-error reproduction, Tenzer et al.)rank-2 + sparse error pairs sparse support: empty (fraction 0.000); decomposition converged; relative residual 0.187; resulting weights identical to refit IU-PCR (cosine 1.000) The sparse mechanism has nothing to capture. The residual dependence is diffuse, not localized in a few pairs; SU-PCR degenerates to IU-PCR here.
Conditional independence given the label (the classical one-factor / SML reading)correlation is caused by the target mean |off-diag ρ|: marginal 0.484 → conditional 0.479 (y=0) / 0.498 (y=1) inside error traces Violated. The shared factor is common uncertainty (redundancy), not the error signal. PC1 ≠ signal direction.
Block / clustered models (clustered U-PCR, family groupings)correlated groups + weak cross-group same-transform 0.87 » same-stream 0.50 ≈ neither 0.45 Supported, with a twist: the natural blocks are the four transforms, not the seven streams. A clustered/grouped fusion at token level should group by transform.
Dependency-embracing fusion (the DEEM / CIW-DEEM line)model the dependence instead of assuming it away the failed conditional-independence check above is precisely its motivation; but the dependency-corrected SDSF ridge on this matrix flips weights (cosine −0.095 vs frozen) and loses every descriptive metric Motivated but delicate. The dependence is real and label-free correction is easy to get wrong; a token-level DEEM arm needs the same care the global 24-cell benchmark got.

Fusion weight vectors and descriptive diagnostics

Read this table as diagnostics, not as a benchmark. All rows are descriptive: the population was historically opened, there is no fold structure, no bootstrap interval, and no preregistered gate. The dedicated frozen localizer of record (the family6 step scorer in the fair-comparison package) is a different, stronger system evaluated under a different metric (ProcessBench macro-F1) and is not comparable to the argmax-token rule used here. Nothing in this document selects or promotes a method.

The pattern worth carrying into the token-head fusion work: the frozen head’s advantage over its own refit (0.543 vs 0.536 token AUROC; 0.329 vs 0.304 exact) comes from its level-heavy weight profile — fit on the Qwen3-4B development population, it happens to weight the transform family that carries the event-like localization signal, while a fresh label-free fit on this population drifts toward the uniform redundancy direction. Any new fusion arm has to beat that failure mode: label-free fits at token level are pulled toward the common factor, which is not the localization signal.

Section 7

Cross-domain glance: RAGTruth-EC pilot

Even saturated, the transplanted evidence carries some token-level signal on the pilot: pooled token AUROC 0.608 over 1,667 tokens (108 span tokens, 8 responses), and 0.592 for the evidence-contrast form (full − noctx). These are pilot-sized descriptive numbers only. The deployed RAG token head is a separate fixed IU-PCR pipeline with its own reference and feature contract (frozen RAGTruth token AUROC 0.6586); a proper token-level RAG analysis should rerun this atlas on ragtruth_ec_full with a domain-fit reference rather than the transplanted ProcessBench one.
